rhythms.notes: Equal quarter-note kicks only. This shared foundation is not itself a complete genre.
rhythms.title: Four to the floor / bare pulse

rhythms.notes: Original swung variant: extra ghost kicks and claps; not a transcription of a named track.
rhythms.title: Jackin house / ghost-kick turnaround

rhythms.notes: A deliberately broken alternative; not all techno uses a quarter-note kick.
rhythms.title: Techno / broken kick study

rhythms.notes: Original three-sixteenth percussion cycle over 4/4: both layers close after three bars.
rhythms.title: Techno / three-step percussion cycle

rhythms.notes: Backbeats on 2/4; the second kick sits on the & of 3. Off-grid hats supply shuffle.
rhythms.title: UK garage / two-step foundation

rhythms.notes: Garage also has a four-to-the-floor branch; it is not all two-step.
rhythms.title: UK garage / four-four shuffle

rhythms.notes: Bass onsets are included as movement cues. Audio uses a simple synth, not a sampled Reese patch.
rhythms.title: Speed garage / offbeat bass answers

rhythms.notes: A 140 BPM syncopated study; grime has no single mandatory snare pattern.
rhythms.title: Grime / displaced snare conversation

rhythms.notes: 3+3+2 sixteenth grouping is not a tuplet: the grid here remains straight.
rhythms.title: UK drill / grouped hats

rhythms.notes: Snare: beat 3 in bar one, beat 4 in bar two. This is one common design, not a rule for all drill.
rhythms.title: UK drill / moving second-bar snare

rhythms.notes: The added hat fill uses rational tuplets; grouped hats and triplet rolls remain distinct concepts.
rhythms.title: UK drill / true triplet hat fill

rhythms.notes: Gregory C. Coleman / The Winstons, Amen, Brother. Four bars, not a generic 2-bar loop. Timing/velocity are approximations; no original recording or measured human microtiming.
rhythms.title: Amen / four-bar structural study

rhythms.notes: A/B study: only quiet snares removed. This deliberately simplified version is not the complete Amen.
rhythms.title: Amen / remove the ghost snares

rhythms.notes: Original chopped-break-style arrangement, not the original Amen sequence.
rhythms.title: Jungle / rearranged break fragments

rhythms.notes: Four-bar original phrase: the final half uses fewer main snares, not a tempo change.
rhythms.title: Jungle / full-time to half-time answer

rhythms.notes: Offbeat bass/pulse is included. A rhythmic sketch cannot supply trance harmony, timbre or arrangement.
rhythms.title: Trance / offbeat lift

rhythms.notes: Quarter-note kick version with offbeat snare answers; one useful dembow foundation, not every dancehall rhythm.
rhythms.title: Reggaeton / dembow answer

rhythms.notes: An original percussion and log-drum-style bass rhythm. Pitched bass is a cue lane, not a downloaded sample.
rhythms.title: Amapiano / shaker and bass-percussion study

amapiano.supports: Slower house-adjacent percussive grooves, shakers and substantial bass activity. Our log-drum-style bass rhythm is an original study.
amapiano.title: What is amapiano music? Its history and how to make it

amen_lesson.supports: Four-bar structure, repeated opening bars, internal snares, displaced closing backbeats and fourth-bar crash.
amen_lesson.title: Amen Break drum lesson

amen_program.supports: Ride eighths, kick doubles, dynamic contrast, later displaced snares, pedal hat; manually programmed timing is not the original performance.
amen_program.title: How to program an Amen-style break

dembow.supports: Dembow quarter kicks and displaced snare answers at 0.75/1.5/2.75/3.5 beats in a 4/4 bar.
dembow.title: What is reggaeton? How to make reggaeton beats that move you

disco.supports: Disco-related acoustic groove possibilities include four-on-floor or a looser first/third-beat kick.
disco.title: Nu-Disco: Live Groove

dnb.supports: DnB two-step kick on first/sixth eighths, snare on 2/4, eighth hats with lighter in-between notes; house and funk examples.
dnb.title: 7 drum patterns every producer should know

drill.supports: UK drill grouped 3+3+2 hats, moving snare, sparse kicks and portamento bass; not a universal rule for all drill.
drill.title: How to make a drill beat with haunting, dark undertones

edm.supports: Straight house/disco, broken electro, rapid jungle/DnB and spacious dubstep half-time; synthesis and arrangement also define genre.
edm.title: How to make electronic music: the ultimate guide

four_floor.supports: Quarter-note kicks with second/fourth-beat backbeats; common house/techno foundation.
four_floor.title: Beat and tempo; Backbeats

garage.supports: Both four-to-the-floor and 2-step; syncopated kicks, backbeats and delayed sixteenth hats.
garage.title: Everything you need to know about UK garage music and how to make it

grime.supports: Grime's approximately 140 BPM grids, displaced/repeated/syncopated snares; trap hat subdivisions.
grime.title: How to program 6 classic hip-hop, trap and grime beats

jack.supports: Four-on-floor with swing, ghost kicks and additional clap/snare activity.
jack.title: Drum programming: Jackin' House

jungle.supports: Chopped breaks, pitched percussive dialogue and jungle rhythmic composition.
jungle.title: Sully: Sketches

rave.supports: Combining break fragments with a four-on-floor kick, without importing that recording or tutorial MIDI.
rave.title: Lo-Fi House & Breaks Fusion

techno.supports: Percussion-heavy repetitive techno production; our grids are independent studies, not the article's exact pattern.
techno.title: Hypnotic Techno Inspired by Phase Fatale's Love Is Destructive
